issues.title: Align the documentation lockup after the Lazurio logo direction is finalized
issues.question: Which final Lazurio lockup should the documentation header use after the in-progress product identity is approved?
issues.impact: The first release safely uses the text title and the approved favicon. It must not present a working lockup direction as final brand identity.
options: Keep the text title until the design-system owner publishes a final asset.
Adopt the approved asset in a later scoped visual update with browser parity checks.

issues.title: Complete post-migration Cloudflare hardening
issues.question: What reviewed sequence should enable DNSSEC and move eligible lazurio.ai hostnames from DNS-only resolution to Cloudflare proxying now that the authoritative cutover has converged?
issues.impact: Cloudflare now owns authoritative DNS and public resolver convergence was verified on 2026-08-26. DNS-only records preserve the previous network path and do not add Cloudflare proxy, WAF or origin shielding to the dashboard or current apex. Enabling proxying before origin TLS and rollback are verified could interrupt service; DNSSEC still requires a separately reviewed, end-to-end activation.
options: Recommended: enable DNSSEC through Cloudflare and WEDOS with end-to-end validation, then proxy the dashboard only after strict origin TLS and a direct-origin protection path are verified.
Keep the dashboard DNS-only until Cloudflare Tunnel or an origin firewall allowlist prevents bypassing the proxy.
Replace the current apex and wildcard only in the separate Lazurio website rollout; do not combine that content cutover with DNS security hardening.

issues.title: Upgrade the Astro runtime family after dependency-alert reachability review
issues.question: Can one reviewed static-site upgrade remove all 18 current GitHub dependency alerts without regressing the deployed Cloudflare Pages contract?
issues.impact: Live GitHub readback on 2026-08-31 identifies 17 Astro advisories and one @astrojs/cloudflare advisory. The replacement draft moves to patched Astro 7.2.9 with its matching official integrations, removes the unused runtime adapter from this static site, preserves the existing accessibility Markdown transform and validates the Pages 302 redirect through local Pages emulation. It remains in progress until the replacement PR is reviewed and merged.
options: Recommended: review and merge the prepared static-site upgrade, then verify that GitHub closes all 18 alerts on the default branch.
Keep the vulnerable runtime temporarily only with an advisory-by-advisory reachability assessment and an explicit short expiry.

issues.title: Re-verify the five Microsoft 365 Copilot sources before their review date
issues.question: Who re-verifies microsoft-copilot-architecture, -data-protection, -privacy, -requirements and -extensibility against current Microsoft Learn before 2026-11-04?
issues.impact: Their reviewDueAt is 2026-11-04. From 2026-11-05 `bun run check` fails on every pull request until the sources are re-verified and their dates moved.
options: Re-verify the five sources against Microsoft Learn and move reviewedAt and reviewDueAt in one pull request.
Retire a source the documentation no longer needs and remove its citations.
decision_needed_for: keeping the documentation check green after 2026-11-04

issues.title: Return the browser test job to ubuntu-latest once Playwright supports Ubuntu 26.04
issues.question: When does the repository upgrade Playwright to a release that installs Chromium on Ubuntu 26.04?
issues.impact: ubuntu-latest became Ubuntu 26.04 and `bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium` fails there with Playwright 1.55, so the verify job's test is pinned to ubuntu-24.04.
options: Upgrade Playwright and unpin the runner in one pull request with green browser tests.
Keep the pin while ubuntu-24.04 runners remain available.
decision_needed_for: the runner image of the verify job

issues.title: Give people a clickable way to name a new device, and let the Admin set the name at approval
issues.question: How does a device get its `<login>-<device>` name when no person-facing step may use a command line?
issues.impact: Tailscale names a node after the system hostname; on phones that is usually only the manufacturer or model. Tailscale for Android 1.104.5 has no name setting (checked in the app on 2026-11-03), and Tailscale documents no clickable name setting for iOS, macOS or Windows; the only documented ways are the CLI flag and the Hostname system policy. guide/tailscale-add-device therefore asks people to tell the Admin the wanted name and says the guide does not yet describe how the Admin sets it.
options: Proposed: the Admin types the agreed name in Dashboard when approving, and the approval sets it on the node; until then the system name stays.

Proposed: Dashboard offers a personal settings file (an Apple configuration profile on macOS, a registry file on Windows) with LoginURL and Hostname, opened by double-click. Needs verification that the policies apply with Headscale and do not lock the device to one tailnet.
Accept the system name and show the owner and device kind next to it in Dashboard.
decision_needed_for: the Device name section and Admin check 3 of guide/tailscale-add-device

issues.title: Confirm that Dashboard shows the login server address and the device approval before the add-device guide is published
issues.question: Does the released Dashboard show a person their Organization's Headscale login server address, and does an Admin approve waiting devices there (today through a reviewed batch change)?
issues.impact: guide/tailscale-add-device tells readers that Dashboard shows the exact address and that Admins approve devices in Dashboard. Both are being built separately; the public access model documents the approval service as the target with a reviewed change as fallback.
options: Publish after the Dashboard change ships and re-read it.
Publish now with the Admin as the source of the address, and add Dashboard once it ships.

issues.title: Windows has no clickable way to enter the Organization's login server
issues.question: How does a person on Windows join their Organization's tailnet without a command line?
issues.impact: Tailscale's documentation says the Windows app cannot add a custom control server in its interface; the documented alternatives are the CLI and the LoginURL registry value. The guide now tells Windows users to ask their Admin for help, which does not scale.
options: Proposed: Dashboard offers a ready registry file with LoginURL (and Hostname) for the person's Organization, applied by double-click and confirmed by Windows.
Proposed: Lazurio provides a small signed installer that installs Tailscale with the Organization's LoginURL.
Keep the Admin-assisted step.

issues.title: Add own screenshots for iPhone and macOS to the add-device guide
issues.question: Where can the iPhone and macOS steps be photographed without a signed-in account and without personal data on screen?
issues.impact: The Android steps have own screenshots from Tailscale 1.104.5. iPhone and macOS have none: Tailscale's documentation images carry no licence that allows reuse, so the guide links to them, and the available Mac is a personal machine whose screen may show private data. The macOS Option-click path (Debug → Custom Login Server → Add Account…) comes from the Headscale documentation and is unverified in the current app.
options: Take them on a test iPhone and a test Mac with no Tailscale account.
Have the reviewer take them on their own devices, cropped to the Tailscale window, before publication.
decision_needed_for: the iPhone and macOS sections of guide/tailscale-add-device
